sections.title: Tree and flowers
sections.text: Syzygium jambos, the rose apple, is a small evergreen tree that reaches about 10 m and forms a dense, spreading crown. Its opposite leaves are glossy and can be 9–26 cm long. Large, pom-pom-like flower clusters are 5–10 cm wide and have many conspicuous stamens.

sections.title: Fruit and food
sections.text: The whitish to yellow, round or egg-shaped fruit is about 2.5–5 cm wide, often smells of rosewater and contains a stone. The fruit is eaten raw or cooked. It is distinct from red-fruited S. malaccense and the smaller water apple, S. aqueum.

sections.title: Plate
sections.text: The plate shows the creamy flower stamens and pale, rose-scented fruit used to distinguish this rose apple from its close relatives.
